newsitem.title: FRANCE: Prosecutor slams weekly on dead Mitterrand photos.
newsitem.headline: Prosecutor slams weekly on dead Mitterrand photos.

text.p: A prosecutor urged a Paris court on Monday to punish the weekly Paris Match for publishing two photographs of the late French President Francois Mitterrand, snapped secretly as he lay on his death bed.
Speaking at a hearing on a complaint by Mitterrand's family, deputy prosecutor Francois Cordier asked the court to rule that publication of the clandestine photos had "gone over the limit".
An attorney for the magazine, Paul Lombard, countered that Paris Match was simply fulfilling its journalistic obligations.
The Mitterrand family is seeking a symbolic one franc (20 cents) in damages for each member of the family. It also wants an apology printed on the magazine's cover.
The court said it would rule on the matter on January 13.
Mitterrand's family filed suit in January against "persons unknown" in an effort to discover who took the photographs, alleging they violated the family's privacy.
The two photographs showed Mitterrand's body, dressed in a dark suit and tie and hands crossed on his stomach, in the Paris apartment where he died.
Mitterrand died on January 8, about eight months after he left office following two seven-year terms as head of state.
Paris Match, in an editorial, said at the time, "We take responsibility for these documents because their beauty, their strength, their weight makes them essential".
It has declined to name the photographer.

In a statement issued in January, Mitterrand's three children, his widow Danielle and his companion Anne Pingeot said publishing the photos was immoral and "runs counter to the respect due to the dead".
